result.summary: This pull request refactors the bitcoinkernel logging API to deliver structured log entries (btck_LogEntry) containing raw metadata and message slices instead of pre-formatted strings. It simplifies the C logging configuration to level filtering, introduces an internal KernelLogger, and drops the dependency on logging.cpp from the kernel build.
result.problem: Downstream consumers of libbitcoinkernel had to parse formatted text strings to extract timestamps, source locations, log levels, and categories. In addition, the kernel library depended directly on node-specific logging machinery like logging.cpp.

resolved_concerns: ajtowns flagged indirection overhead and argument evaluation regressions for LogInfo, leading to the removal of std::function dispatchers and the preservation of eager argument evaluation.

purpleKarrot questioned the necessity of multiple logging connections and the singleton design; the author clarified that connection scoping matches the existing API while keeping client filtering lightweight.

w0xlt identified exception-safety and lock-inversion deadlock hazards during callback registration and destruction, which the author fixed using RAII wrappers and releasing locks before user-data cleanup.

result.card: PR #34374 upgrades the libbitcoinkernel logging API from string formatting to structured log entries (btck_LogEntry) and removes the dependency on logging.cpp from the kernel library. This resolves the awkward requirement for external kernel consumers to parse timestamps, levels, and source locations out of formatted strings. The approach has strong support from ryanofsky, and earlier concerns regarding indirection overhead and locking edge cases from ajtowns and w0xlt have been resolved. The PR is clean, passes CI, and is ready for final review.
